# Universities and student email domains

<!-- GENERATED by backend/tools/universities/generate.py. Edit backend/data/universities_bd.json instead. -->

Campus Saga accepts a student only with their **university email** (email
code or university Google account). This page lists every university we
recognise and the email domains that map to it.

- **169 universities** (61 public, 108 private), **232 sign-in domains**
- Researched 2026-10-27 from the University Grants Commission (UGC) lists and each university's own website
- Source of truth: [`backend/data/universities_bd.json`](../backend/data/universities_bd.json) (with source links per university)

## How matching works

1. The email's domain is matched against the sign-in domains **and all their subdomains**: `rafi@cse.du.ac.bd` → `du.ac.bd` → University of Dhaka.
2. The **longest** match wins, so a department or student subdomain never falls through to a different university.
3. Matching is on whole labels: `x@nottest.ac.bd` never matches `test.ac.bd`.
4. Shared suffixes (`ac.bd`, `edu.bd`) and free mail (`gmail.com`, `yahoo.com` …) can never be added. The database refuses them.

## Common patterns

### Website domain endings

| Ending | Public | Private |
|---|---|---|
| `.ac.bd` | 38 | 47 |
| `.edu.bd` | 16 | 51 |
| `.edu` | 2 | 6 |
| `.ac` | 0 | 2 |
| `.com` | 0 | 1 |

### Student email subdomains (under the website domain)

|---|---|
| `student.` | 18 |
| `std.` | 5 |
| `stud.` | 2 |
| `stu.` | 2 |
| `g.` | 1 |
| `ugrad.` | 1 |
| one per department or programme | 3: United International University (14), University of Dhaka (6), Bangladesh University of Engineering & Technology (2) |

### What this means

- **Public universities:** 38 of 56 websites end in `.ac.bd`; the rest mostly `.edu.bd`.
- **Private universities:** 51 of 107 use `.edu.bd` and 47 use `.ac.bd`.
- **Plain international endings:** `aiub.edu`, `aust.edu`, `diu.ac`, `ewubd.edu`, `grameenu.ac`, `iubat.edu`, `juniv.edu`, `northsouth.edu`, `sust.edu`, `timesuniversitybd.com`, `uap-bd.edu`.
- **Students usually get a subdomain** of the website domain (`student.`, `std.`, `stud.`, `g.`, `ugrad.`, or one per department or programme, like UIU's `bscse.uiu.ac.bd`). The subdomain rule covers these automatically, so for most universities **the website domain alone is enough**. We found student-domain evidence for 59 universities; for the rest the website domain covers students who use it.
- **The exceptions matter:** some universities give students a different domain than their website, or were renamed and still receive mail on the old domain (aliases). These are listed explicitly; without them those students could not sign in.
- **Look-alike abbreviations are common** (`diu.edu.bd` Daffodil vs `diu.ac` Dhaka International; `sau.edu.bd` vs `sau.ac.bd`; `bmu.ac.bd` vs `bmu.edu.bd`). Always add exact domains; never guess from an abbreviation.

## Gaps to fill

- **No domain yet** (students cannot sign in until one is added): Eco University of Science and Technology, Lakshmipur Science & Technology University, Meherpur University, Narayanganj Science and Technology University, Shariatpur Agricultural University, Thakurgaon University
- **Held back, needs verification:** Green University of Bangladesh (`student.green.ac.bd`)
- When a student reports "my university email doesn't work", check their domain, add it to the JSON, and generate a new migration.
